---
title: "Cohort-driven, assay-aware thalassaemia genotyping"
abstract: |
  This thesis combines a retrospective molecular-testing cohort with an explicit
  computational model of ONT amplicon observability. The cohort work defines the
  locally relevant HBA/HBB genotype and phenotype questions. NanoGlobin compiles
  declared primer designs against chromosome-haplotype sequences, classifies
  observed molecules, and ranks the diploid haplotype states that can explain
  those products. Analytical accuracy is evaluated only where an appropriate
  truth source exists.
---

```{r}
source("R/setup.R")
```

# Thesis question

Can a canonical chromosome-haplotype and evidence representation unify the
retrospective thalassaemia records, support genotype--phenotype and database
analyses, expose assay-dependent blind spots, and drive an open ONT amplicon
genotyper?

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Historical and ONT reports] --> B[Canonical genotype and evidence ledger]
  B --> C[Reported HBA/HBB landscape]
  B --> D[HBA x HBB phenotype analysis]
  C --> E[Sequence-resolved candidate haplotypes]
  E --> F[Declared assay compiler]
  F --> G[Primer-aware molecule evidence]
  G --> H[Candidate haplotype posterior]
  H --> I[Resolved, ambiguous, or no-call]
  I --> J[Independent adjudication]
```

# Draft status

This Quarto book is a live analysis and writing workspace. It renders to HTML for
rapid review and to a Typst PDF for submission-oriented typesetting. Patient-level
source data and reports must remain outside the repository; chapters consume only
approved de-identified tables or committed synthetic examples.
